pages.title: Pit Kiln
pages.text: §3Pit Kiln§r is the core facility for ancient pottery firing. It uses a dirt-walled pit structure, burning fuel through the fire mouth to produce high temperatures, combined with vents to control the kiln atmosphere, transforming greenware into different ceramic products.$(br2)This guide will walk you step by step through the construction and firing process of the pit kiln.

pages.title: Firing Process
pages.text: The pit kiln operates in five stages:$(br)$(li)§5Build the Kiln§r — Place pit kiln block, surround with dirt in a U-shape$(br)$(li)§5Install Grate & Load§r — Install grate, place greenware inside$(br)$(li)§5Seal & Heat§r — Add fuel, seal with kiln lid, ignite$(br)$(li)§5High-Temp Firing§r — Temperature exceeds 100℃, formal firing begins$(br)$(li)§5Cooling & Collect§r — Fuel depletes, temperature drops, products auto-drop on completion

pages.title: Key Concepts
pages.text: $(li)§3Temperature§r: Determined by fuel, grate efficiency, and insulation grade, max 900℃ (1200℃ with blowpipe)$(br)$(li)§3Oxygen Content§r: Controlled by fire mouth and vent states$(br)$(li)§3Oxidizing Atmosphere§r: High oxygen, suitable for §4redware$(br)$(li)§3Reducing Atmosphere§r: Low oxygen, suitable for §3gray ware§0 and §8black ware$(br)$(li)§3Insulation Grade§r: Determined by surrounding dirt blocks (0-4 sides)

pages.title: Step 1: Gather Raw Materials
pages.text: $(li)Use §4Flint Shovel§r on sand/gravel to get §4Raw Clay§r$(br)$(li)Use §4Flint Knife§r on grass to get §4Grass Fiber§r$(br)$(li)Harvest wheat for §4Rice Husk§r (30% chance)$(br2)These are the basic materials for pottery.
§3Mixed Clay Recipe§r$(br2)Craft: §4Raw Clay + Any Temper (Grog/Sand/Red Sand) + Grass Fiber§r$(br2)Mixed clay is the foundation for all pottery greenware items.

pages.title: Step 2: Make Greenware
pages.text: Shape mixed clay into greenware:$(br2)$(li)§4Crucible§r — for melting metals$(br)$(li)§4Mold§r — for casting shapes$(br)$(li)§4Brick§r — for construction$(br)$(li)§4Blowpipe§r — for metalworking$(br2)§4Tip:§r The temper material in the mixed clay recipe can be substituted with §3Sand§r or §3Red Sand§r — no need for specialized temper grog. Greenware must be fired in a kiln to become usable.

pages.title: Step 3: Build and Fire Kiln
pages.text: Building a complete pit kiln requires:$(br2)$(li)Pit kiln block ×1$(br)$(li)Dirt blocks ×8 (for kiln body)$(br)$(li)Fire mouth block ×1$(br)$(li)Grate block ×1$(br)$(li)Kiln lid ×1$(br)$(li)Fire drill ×1 (ignition tool)$(br)$(li)Fuel (firewood, straw, rice husk char, etc.)$(br)$(li)Greenware items$(br2)Procedure: Use §4Flint Shovel§r on dirt to dig kiln pit → load greenware → add fuel through fire mouth → seal with kiln lid & ignite → control temp and atmosphere → wait for firing to complete.

pages.title: Firing Conditions
pages.text: Different products need different firing conditions:$(br2)$(li)§4Redware§r (oxidizing atmosphere): Red Mold, Red Brick$(br)$(li)§3Gray Ware§r (reducing atmosphere): Gray Crucible$(br)$(li)§8Black Ware§r (strong reducing atmosphere): Advanced ceramics$(br2)§4Tip:§r Vents control oxygen levels inside the kiln. Close the fire mouth tightly to create a reducing atmosphere.
§3Gray Crucible§r is one of the key successful products. Fired in a reducing atmosphere, it has high temperature resistance and is the basic tool for metal smelting.
§4Red Mold§r is fired in an oxidizing atmosphere, used for casting metal ingots and tools.
